svg.aria-label: What to expect at 4K: how much less time FSR 4 takes per frame with this project's builds than with AMD's own, card by card, moving scene, Balanced. RX 7800 XT, Linux (this project): exact 37%, lossy 55% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 2%, 4.1.2l-lossy 18% less than AMD's Lite. RX 7900 XT, Windows (1 report): exact 18%, lossy 34% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 6%, 4.1.2l-lossy 5% less than AMD's Lite. RX 7800 XT, Windows (1 report): exact 9%, lossy 27% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 6%, 4.1.2l-lossy 11% less than AMD's Lite. RX 7600, Windows (2 reports): exact 30%, lossy 41% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 5%, 4.1.2l-lossy 10% less than AMD's Lite. RX 6900 XT, Windows (1 report): exact 4%, lossy 19% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 2%, 4.1.2l-lossy 13% less than AMD's Lite. RX 6800 XT, Windows (1 report): exact 5%, lossy 19% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 4%, 4.1.2l-lossy 13% less than AMD's Lite. RX 6800, Windows (2 reports): exact 2%, lossy 16% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 7%, 4.1.2l-lossy 11% less than AMD's Lite. RX 6750 XT, Windows (4 reports): exact 2%, lossy 16% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 7%, 4.1.2l-lossy 11% less than AMD's Lite. RX 6700 XT, Windows (6 reports): exact 2%, lossy 16% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 8%, 4.1.2l-lossy 11% less than AMD's Lite. RX 6700, Windows (2 reports): exact 3%, lossy 16% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 7%, 4.1.2l-lossy 12% less than AMD's Lite. RX 6650 XT, Windows (1 report): exact 4%, lossy 18% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 6%, 4.1.2l-lossy 12% less than AMD's Lite. RX 6600 XT, Windows (1 report): exact 4%, lossy 18% less time than AMD's FSR 4.1.2; 4.1.2l-exact 6%, 4.1.2l-lossy 12% less than AMD's Lite. The Windows rows come from testers' timing-kit reports of test builds with this release's shaders. Other resolutions give other numbers.
svg.text: How much less time FSR 4 takes per frame than with AMD's own. Longer is faster.
This project's RX 7800 XT, Linux (Proton): the release's builds
Windows, testers' timing-kit reports (test builds with this release's shaders; median per card)
Moving scene, 4K output, Balanced. AMD's FSR 4.1.2 is the card's own model: on RX 7000 it gives FSR 4.1.1's picture, on RX 6000 a picture that
differs only in rounding. Linux row: AMD's FSR 4.1.2 = its FSR SDK 2.4.0 game DLL; Lite in this project's local test harness; two runs each.
Windows rows: mostly test builds (lossy with test weights, same speed; RX 6000 exact and some RX 7000 reports without AMD's SDK pass 11, which
this release's exact DLLs add: up to 3% at 4K so far); reports of the release's own timing kit time its DLLs. 1080p, 1440p and other cards:
the tables below. Linux gains do not carry over to Windows.
The two panels have different scales: 0 to 60% on the left, 0 to 20% on the right.
